paragraphs.text: King Solomon’s solemn offering at Gibeon, 2Ch 1:1-6. His choice of wisdom is blessed by God, 2Ch 1:7-12. His strength and wealth, 1Ch 1:13-17.
or established, after his seditious brother Adonijah and his partisans were suppressed; and he was received with the universal consent and joy of his princes and people.
to wit, concerning his intention of going to Gibeon, and that they should attend him thither, as the next verse shows.
upon which the tabernacle was placed; whence it is called the great high place, 1Ki 3:4.
He separated the ark from the tabernacle, and brought it to Jerusalem, because there he intended to build a far more noble and lasting habitation for it.

either Moses, mentioned 2Ch 1:3, or Bezaleel, here last named, by the command and direction of Moses; or David, who may be said to put it there, because he continued it there, and did not remove it, as he did the ark from the tabernacle.
i.e. sought the Lord and his favour by hearty prayers and sacrifices in the place which God had appointed for that work, Lev 17:3,4.

i.e. Which altar. But that he had now said, 2Ch 1:5, and therefore would not unnecessarily repeat it. Or rather, who; and so these words are emphatical, and contain a reason why Solomon went thither, because the Lord was there graciously present to hear prayers and receive sacrifices.
in a dream, of which See Poole "1Ki 3:5", &c.
What one man is sufficient to govern so numerous a people?
i.e. the taking away of their lives.
or, from the high place; for the Hebrew prefix lamed, which commonly signifies to, is sometimes put for the Latin de, which signifies from.
Of this and the three following verses, See Poole "1Ki 10:26", &c.
